_comment: WC2026 SEMI-FINAL (M101: France, QF97 winner, vs Spain, QF98 winner), 2026-07-14 -- the tournament's marquee tie: two 94-rated giants, the two best defences AND the two most clinical attacks left. MEASURED PROFILES (6 matches each): FRANCE -- GF 16 / GA 3 (all conceded in the group), THREE straight knockout clean sheets (3-0 Sweden, 1-0 Paraguay, 2-0 Morocco), closes every knockout in 90', the most in-form side in the draw. SPAIN -- GF 11 / GA 1 (best defensive record: five straight clean sheets, then 1 conceded to Belgium's firing attack), grinds elite opponents and STRIKES LATE (two straight late deciders: 1-0 Portugal, 2-1 Belgium). Style collision: France's production (2.67 GF/game) vs Spain's near-impenetrability (0.17 GA/game); both defences are GENUINELY elite vs quality (the Spain-Portugal vs Mexico-England A/B lesson: real defensive records transfer) -> a TIGHT, LOW-scoring, tense semi (total 2.25, Under 2.5 at 61%, BTTS mild-No 53.5%) with the FATTEST deep tail of the tournament (ET 30.8%, pens 17.0%) -- near-even + low-scoring = the lottery zone. France the THIN favourite: equal ratings, but more firepower (16 vs 11), a cleaner path profile (closes in 90'; Spain needs late goals), and Spain's aura of invincibility already dented by Belgium. BTTS decision: both attacks are real (never zero either) but both defences elite -> mild BTTS-No, both clean-sheet branches live (FRA 35%, ESP 30%). CONCLUSIVE BOTTOM LINE (per the standing note, graded strictly): THE CALL -- France advance IN 90 MINUTES, by a single goal, in a game that is level or scoreless deep into the second half (thin edge: advancement only 54.3/45.7). THE SCORELINE -- France 1-0 (tied-2nd modal at 11.6%; the modal 1-1 is a draw, and France's knockout profile is the clean-sheet 90'-closer). THE MARKETS -- 1X2: France (thin, 38.4 vs 30.9); Under 2.5 (solid, 60.9%); BTTS-No (thin, 53.5%). Risk to the call: Spain's late-strike pattern makes the final 20 minutes the danger zone, and the 31% ET branch is the single most likely spoiler of the manner. Home = France (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.result: France 0-2 Spain. SPAIN advance to the FINAL; France go to the third-place match. Spain shut out the tournament's most productive attack (France's first blank in seven games) and won in 90' -- their SIXTH clean sheet in seven matches.
_postmatch.model_1x2: France 38.4 / Draw 30.8 / Spain 30.9 (LOW, 90'); advancement France 54.3 / Spain 45.7. BOTTOM LINE (committed): France 1-0 in 90', Under 2.5, BTTS-No.
_postmatch.grade: ❌ MISS under the strict rubric -- the committed side (France) was eliminated. Graded separately: the DISTRIBUTION was honest and the committed MARKETS both landed (Under 2.5 ✅ -- two goals; BTTS-No ✅ -- France blanked; 'tight, low-scoring, clean-sheet-decides' was exactly the game). The call simply picked the wrong side of a declared 54/46 coin-flip: Spain winning in 90' was priced at 30.9% and the game settled in regulation (the 69% branch). A 46% underdog advancing is not a tail event -- it is the other side of the coin.
_postmatch.verdict: The texture read was right and the side read was wrong -- and the miss is instructive. I made France the thin favourite on FIREPOWER (GF 16 vs 11) and the 90'-closer profile; Spain won on the signal I under-weighted: their defence (GA 1 in six, now 2 conceded-in-seven with SIX clean sheets) was the single most predictive stat in the tournament, and it beat the best attack left. Spain didn't even need their late-strike pattern -- they controlled and won 2-0, blanking a France side that had scored in all six games. When the tournament's best defence met the tournament's best attack, DEFENCE TRAVELLED. The model had this near even (54/46) and the market agreed -- the process was sound -- but where I spent my one committed pick, the tie-breaker criterion (attacking production) was the weaker signal versus defensive record vs quality.
_postmatch.lesson: TIE-BREAKER RULE for near-even elite ties: when two giants are within a few points of a coin-flip, break the tie toward the ELITE DEFENCE, not the elite attack. Rationale now empirical: Spain's GA-1 record kept transferring all tournament (six clean sheets in seven, including blanking France's GF-16 attack), while attacking production is streakier game-to-game. Related: 'closes in 90-minutes' is a WINNER's profile stat, not a predictor of WHO wins -- the game did settle in 90' as called, just for the other side. First ❌ of the conclusive-calls era: the distribution and markets were right, the committed side was wrong -- exactly the failure mode the rubric was designed to expose rather than hide behind 'the favourite was priced fine'.
